questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
- Feeling like there would not be that much of a change in the every day life in regards to culture and how things work. 
- The opportunities to do other things and explore when not studying.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Medium. If you make an effort it is not that hard, but you have to do a lot of research yourself to be sure you have all the necessary information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a mandatory introduction week for all international students where we got information about the most important things.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy. The university has some links with recommendations for student housing on their website. I found a student lodge through one of the links and then just made a reservation of a room. However, I booked well in advance which is necessary to be sure not all rooms are booked.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: A student lodge is a very good choice! It will be easy to get in contact with other students, both international and locals.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to fill in a personal information, upload a photo and sign some documents.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was always possible to write an email to the responsible person at the international office at the host university.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful. I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do not wait until the last minute in case any problems occur.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses is ok, and all the subjects are recognizable from what is learned at KU. However, the work load is way heavier than at KU, especially when being a master student, we are not used to making assignment and having exercise classes anymore.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very small classes with few people, working on school computers in programming courses, exercise classes is just the teaching assistant giving all the answers.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Resource Economics, Organizational Economics, Mathematical Methods in Economics, Empirical Macroeconomics II, Environmental Econometrics, Banking Theory.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Depends on what you want. The ones at 4.5 credits usually does not require that much trough the semester, but even at 4.5 credits the exams are tough. The ones at 6 credits have many assignments that takes a lot of time trough the semester, but typically no exams and instead a term paper to hand in.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Schweiz is not as expensive as people say when it comes to grocery shopping compared to the high prices in Danmark. Going out to eat is a bit more expensive, but still affordable. However, public transport is really expensive unless you are under 25 or get the half fare ticket.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: almost every sport

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: uni sport

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the mountains! take advantage of the beautiful nature and that it is only a short train ride away. and during winter, go skiing.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: it takes a lot as the swiss are very reserved, most of them do not even talk to each other during class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: very helpful and easy to adjust to.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- make the most of the weekend and go explore!
- live in a student lodge
- show up to the classes

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The very friendly people I met and got to explore the country with. Experiencing the beautiful nature of Schweiz.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: the exam period only being one week with no breaks to prepare..

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
